model.name: One-qubit finite-temperature Lindblad model
model.hamiltonian: H/hbar = pi * [-detuning_MHz Z + drive_MHz (cos(phase) X + sin(phase) Y)] per microsecond
model.detuning_convention: device frequency minus source frequency; frequency sweep x is source minus device in MHz
model.pulse_convention: Ramsey: +half, free, +half with analysis phase; echo: +half, free/2, +pi, free/2, -half with analysis phase.
model.initial_state: Thermal equilibrium density matrix at the inspected temperature
model.measurement_uncertainty: 95% pointwise Wilson score interval for assignment-channel binomial probability; fixed physical settings and independent shots

sources.title: QuTiP Lindblad master equation and assumptions

limitations: Synthetic one-device two-level rotating-wave model; no hardware execution or manufacturer calibration.
Markovian thermal amplitude damping and pure dephasing; excludes leakage, non-Markovian noise, crosstalk and resonator dynamics.
Cryostat is an explicit elapsed-time exponential approximation; temperature is frozen during each acquisition and the state is thermally reset before each point.
Declared coupling converts attenuated source power to drive; finite square pulses include detuning and decoherence. Pi duration is user configured, never automatically calibrated.
Readout is a state-independent binary confusion channel plus independent binomial shot noise; counts do not include amplifier waveforms or acquisition latency.
Subdivision is a floating-point consistency diagnostic using the same exponential method, not independent solver validation or an estimate of physical-model error.
Discrete exact sample predictions can miss oscillations between points; plotted interpolation is not an additional simulation.
Per-point 95% Wilson intervals describe finite independent binomial sampling of the assignment-channel probability, not uncertainty in the physical model; they are not simultaneous confidence bands.
